episodes.title: Jehovah’s Witnesses Were Right About Blood— Sort of
episodes.description:
Sarah Walbolt, a former Jehovah’s Witness, shares her journey from life inside the Jehovah’s Witness organization to becoming a nurse and recognized global leader in Patient Blood Management (PBM).

Inspired by her father’s survival through bloodless medicine, Sarah reveals how PBM offers evidence-based, blood transfusion alternatives that respect patient choice—very different from the rigid Jehovah’s Witness blood doctrine. She compares the JW bloodless care program with PBM, explains the ethics of blood transfusion refusal for adults and children, and highlights the importance of informed consent healthcare and having a durable power of attorney. 

Sarah also opens up about Jehovah’s Witness misogyny, her healing journey from religious trauma, and how she now empowers patient autonomy and blood management.

Sometimes it starts with small things like feeling afraid to speak up, being rewarded for staying quiet, or slowly losing touch with who you are. It’s subtle, but over time, it can chip away at confidence, peace of mind, and even your sense of identity.

This video explores how toxic work cultures can mirror high-control environments and how those unspoken rules can impact mental health more than most people realize. If burnout, self-doubt, or emotional disconnection have become the norm at work, this might help connect the dots.

And if the question “Am I really in control of my choices?” has ever come up, it’s worth watching until the end.
